author: blu
body: emit-list-eff-base appends the four-instruction selection: preg is the register holding the list pointer and is REPLACED by the effective base (phantom q for a view, unchanged for a plain list); scratch is clobbered. Call it only after every header read of preg is done, because afterwards preg no longer points at a header.

author: blu
body: rdi = list. Returns a view whose length is one less (floored at zero) and whose phantom base is the caller's effective base plus eight, which skips exactly one element whether the input was plain or itself a view. Allocates three cells from R10; inside a deck-record extent R10 is the deck, the same rule every list literal follows.

author: blu
body: Phase-discipline twin of __list_snoc that allocates from the deck pointer instead of the bivy bump pointer R10. The body mirrors __list_snoc; the only differences are (a) the prologue saves R14 and loads deck-pos into it, (b) every R10 reference in the alloc paths is replaced with R14, and (c) every return is preceded by writing R14 back to the deck-pos cell and restoring R14 from the stack. R10 (bivy) is untouched throughout, so a snoc that fires path-3 leaves the bivy bump pointer where it was -- only the deck grows. emit-apply for `list-push` dispatches here when st.deck-bound is True at the call site.

author: blu
body: Phase-discipline twin of __list_append. Always allocates a fresh result list in the deck region (via R14-saved deck-pos cell) and copies a then b into it. The bivy in-place fast path from __list_append is intentionally dropped: when a is in bivy and the bivy is about to be struck, an in-place extend would dangle; when a is in deck, copy-realloc is correct. emit-binary-op for IrAppendList dispatches here when st.deck-bound is True at the call site.

author: blu
body: Guarded on the strength of the shape rather than of a firing, which is stated because it is the weaker evidence: `list-insert-at` reaches the same unchecked scale-and-store as `list-set-at` and was never fired past the end. The tests fire it now.

author: blu
body: The write goes through the effective base so a view stores into its backing, and the function still returns the view it was handed -- the same in-place-and-return-receiver contract plain lists get. The selection runs on a copy in rcx because rdi must survive to be the return value.
